uncited: LRU Cache Management for Octree Nodes is a demand-based page replacement algorithm used to manage the caching of octree nodes in out-of-core volume rendering systems.
It solves the problem of efficiently managing limited in-core memory by prioritizing the retention of recently accessed nodes, thereby optimizing memory reuse.
The method manages a cache of octree nodes using a queue organized in temporal order.
The implementation involves an out-of-core octree controller and an out-of-core point set controller.
*   **Output:** The requested octree node (if present or newly loaded); updated cache state; asynchronous load requests for point sets associated with leaf nodes.
*   **Cache Queue:** A doubly-linked list or similar structure containing all cached octree nodes.
The head represents the most recently used (MRU) node, and the tail represents the least recently used (LRU) node.
*   Check if the node is already present in the cache queue.
*   Identify the node at the tail of the queue (the least recently used node).
*   Evict this node from the cache and free its memory.
*   The out-of-core octree controller retrieves the point list associated with the accessed leaf node.
*   The point set controller checks if the points in the list are already cached in-core.
*   **Cache Size:** Not given in the sources.
This is the generic baseline algorithm described above.
It is considered the most generic among the four out-of-core algorithms evaluated in the source study, containing a very limited amount of application-specific logic.
*   **Time Complexity:** Assuming a doubly-linked list with a hash map for lookup, hit/miss checks and updates are O(1).
*   **Memory Complexity:** O(N) where N is the number of cached nodes.
The LRU strategy for octree nodes was adapted from operating systems, where it is a commonly used demand-based page replacement algorithm.
It was presented by D. Chisnall, M. Chen, and C. Hansen in the context of knowledge-based out-of-core algorithms for data management in visualization.
